title: AURA — Sound, shaped around you

creativeDirection.objective: Create desire for a fictional premium wireless headphone by revealing its form, materials and tactile details without relying on feature claims.
creativeDirection.audience: Design-conscious listeners who respond to considered product design and cinematic product films.
creativeDirection.concept: A material highlight becomes the thread that reveals a sculptural headphone: first its edge, then its silhouette, then its interface and internal construction, before it settles into a quiet hero frame.

visualSystem.typography: Restrained editorial sans-serif; short uppercase phrases with generous tracking and no persistent chapter labels.
visualSystem.composition: Begin with asymmetric macro crops, open into a full three-quarter product view, isolate one interface detail, then return to a shifted wide hero with negative space.
visualSystem.lighting: Soft cool key, controlled warm rim, narrow moving highlights and readable dark surfaces.
visualSystem.textureAndMaterials: Satin polymer, brushed aluminium, soft-touch ear cushions and fine acoustic perforations.

creativeDirection.motionLanguage: One controlled macro push, a short orbiting reveal, a lateral detail move, a brief exploded construction view and a final camera move that settles into stillness. Cuts follow shape and highlight continuity.
creativeDirection.soundDirection: Original restrained electronic pulse throughout, one brushed-metal texture at the opening, one tactile control click at the interface close-up and one low, quiet impact on the final reveal. No voice-over.
assumptions: The product and AURA brand are fictional, created only for this visual benchmark.
The 20-second duration, 1920×1080 frame and 30 fps delivery are fixed.
The 3D model is a stylized design interpretation, not a representation of a real commercial product.
rightsAndFactualConstraints: All 3D geometry is original procedural artwork authored in this repository.
All music and Foley are original deterministic audio fixtures generated by scripts/generate-audio-fixtures.ts.
Do not include real product specifications, endorsements, compatibility claims or availability claims.

renderStrategy.rationale: The story depends on real 3D headphone geometry, physically based materials, close-up camera paths, an exploded construction beat and a controlled hero camera. ProjectVideo's fixed 2D scene schema cannot express these spatial shots.
requiredCapabilities: Physically based metal, polymer and cushion materials
Shot-specific 3D object motion and exploded components
Local synchronized music and Foley tracks
renderStrategy.fallback: If the headless WebGL render is unstable, preserve the storyboard and use a single-concurrency software WebGL render. Do not silently downgrade to ProjectVideo or flatten the 3D product into title cards.

shots.purpose: Create curiosity through a tactile, incomplete view of the product before revealing its identity.
shots.visual: An extreme diagonal macro of the brushed-metal headband connector and earcup yoke, nearly disappearing into graphite shadow.
shots.action: The camera advances along the metal edge while a narrow cool highlight travels across the machined surface.
shots.visualProgression: Start: a small silver edge emerges from near-black. Development: the moving highlight reveals the brushed finish and the curved yoke. End: the line of metal fills the frame and becomes the shape-match cue for the next shot.
shots.framing: Extreme close-up, diagonal crop, shallow visual emphasis on the right-side yoke.
shots.cameraMovement: Short, controlled macro push-in with a slight lateral drift.
shots.transition: Hard match cut on the bright curved metal edge into the full headband arc.
shots.audio: The original score enters softly; a single metallic brush texture follows the highlight sweep.
shots.implementationNotes: Keep most of the headphone outside the frame; no title-card opening.

shots.purpose: Reveal the recognizable silhouette and establish the headphone as the film's central object.
shots.visual: The complete over-ear headphone floats in a restrained mineral studio, shown in a three-quarter view with both earcups and the arched headband clearly readable.
shots.visualMethod: Procedural Three.js product animation with physically based materials.
shots.action: The headphone rotates through a measured three-quarter presentation as the camera makes a short orbit and eases back.
shots.visualProgression: Start: the macro edge resolves into one side of the headband. Development: the arch, sliders and both earcups become visible as the object turns. End: the full silhouette settles into a clear, balanced three-quarter composition.
shots.framing: Medium-wide product shot, three-quarter angle, complete silhouette with breathing room.
shots.cameraMovement: Smooth 20-degree orbit impression with a gentle dolly-out.
shots.transition: Shape-match cut from the circular earcup rim to the control detail.
shots.audio: The score opens slightly; no generic transition effect.
shots.implementationNotes: Keep the headphone identity, proportions and materials consistent in all later shots.

shots.purpose: Give the viewer one tactile point of attention after the overall form is understood.
shots.visual: A tight asymmetric view of the right earcup, showing the control dial, fine perforations and soft cushion edge.
shots.visualMethod: Procedural Three.js 3D close-up and composited typography.
shots.action: The camera slides laterally across the earcup face while the control dial turns a few degrees and catches a thin highlight.
shots.visualProgression: Start: the control is partly hidden by the crop. Development: the sideways camera move brings the dial and acoustic perforations into view. End: the dial rests in a crisp close-up for a short tactile hold.
shots.framing: Tight close-up, shallow angle across the right earcup face.
shots.cameraMovement: Short lateral slider move, then a deliberate hold.
shots.transition: Hard cut on the control click to the separated earcup components.
shots.audio: A quiet original mechanical click lands on the control movement; the music remains restrained.
shots.implementationNotes: Do not imply real touch controls, ports or technical specifications beyond the visible fictional design.

shots.purpose: Add a visual surprise and reward the close inspection without turning the film into a technical specification display.
shots.visual: The right earcup opens into a clean exploded composition: outer plate, trim ring and stylized acoustic driver separate along the cup axis while the headband and opposite cup remain softly present.
shots.action: The earcup's outer elements separate in sequence, pause at distinct depths, then begin returning to alignment.
shots.visualProgression: Start: the assembled earcup holds in close-up. Development: the faceplate, trim and driver separate with measured spacing. End: the components begin to reunite, setting up the complete hero object.
shots.framing: Close-up three-quarter detail with layers separated along the earcup axis.
shots.cameraMovement: Subtle dolly-out to reveal the depth between the components.
shots.transition: Match cut from the reassembling earcup circle to the complete front-facing product.
shots.audio: The score briefly thins to let the component movement breathe; no additional SFX clutter.
shots.implementationNotes: The exploded view is an artistic visualization of the fictional model, not a factual engineering cutaway.

shots.purpose: Resolve the opening material motif with one confident, memorable product frame.
shots.visual: The full headphone settles into a quiet hero composition against near-black graphite, shifted right to leave negative space for the AURA wordmark and short tagline.
shots.visualMethod: Procedural Three.js 3D hero product scene with restrained editorial lockup.
shots.action: The camera eases into a balanced front three-quarter angle as the headphone rotation slows to a complete stop; the wordmark fades in and remains still.
shots.visualProgression: Start: the exploded earcup has returned to the full object. Development: the camera recenters and the product gently settles. End: the headphone and AURA lockup hold cleanly for the final two seconds.
shots.framing: Wide hero shot, product slightly right of centre, generous left-side negative space.
shots.cameraMovement: Slow, short push that eases to a complete stop.
shots.transition: No transition out; hold the final frame to the end.
shots.audio: The score resolves naturally; one quiet low impact marks the hero reveal and leaves a clean tail.
shots.implementationNotes: No price, availability, product specification or call-to-action implying a real product.

acceptanceCriteria: The complete headphone silhouette is clearly revealed by the end of the second shot.
At least three distinct shot scales and compositions are used: macro, full product, close detail and exploded view.
The headphone geometry, material palette and proportions remain coherent across all five shots.
Every shot contains purposeful visible motion; scenes do not merely replace text over a static layout.
The final hero composition holds clearly for at least the final two seconds and resolves the opening material motif.
The original score and three restrained Foley cues support the edit without narration or unsupported product claims.

acceptanceCoverage.rationale: The five-second second shot opens from the headband edge, reveals both earcups and closes on the complete three-quarter silhouette.
